headline: Revenue and EPS grow, but full-year outlook trimmed
summary_short: UHS's Q2 2026 net revenues rose 8.3% y/y to $4.638 billion and diluted EPS grew 10.1% to $5.98, but the company trimmed its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS guidance on Medicaid reimbursement changes.
summary_long: Revenue growth of 8.3% y/y to $4.638B was driven by both segments: Acute Care same-facility revenue +8.2% (admissions +2.9%) and Behavioral Health same-facility revenue +7.4% (admissions +0.5%, pricing +7.1%). Net income of $358.4M included a $72M net favorable item — a $100M Florida Medicaid directed-payment benefit partly offset by a $28M self-insurance reserve increase — versus $101M of favorable Medicaid items a year ago. UHS repurchased $320.3M of stock. Citing Medicaid reimbursement changes and H1 trends, UHS cut FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint 1.9% and Adjusted EPS-diluted guidance midpoint 2.6%, while nudging revenue guidance up 0.2%. Long-term debt rose to $4.9B; cash was roughly flat at $138.8M.

drivers.explanation: Same-facility growth in both segments: Acute Care net revenue +8.2% (admissions +2.9%, revenue per adjusted admission +3.0%) and Behavioral Health +7.4% (admissions +0.5%, revenue per adjusted admission +7.1%).

Reflects the same $72M net favorable pre-tax item described for net income (a $100M Florida Medicaid benefit partly offset by a $28M self-insurance reserve increase), stated as included in operating results.

Included a $72M net favorable pre-tax item ($100M Florida Medicaid directed-payment benefit, partly offset by a $28M self-insurance reserve increase) vs $101M of favorable Medicaid items in the year-ago quarter.
EPS grew faster than net income (+10.1% vs +1.5%) because weighted diluted shares fell to 59.91M from 64.99M on continued buybacks ($320.3M repurchased this quarter).

Management cites 'changes in reimbursements related to certain Medicaid supplemental payment programs' and H1 2026 trends; Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS-diluted guidance midpoints were cut 1.9% and 2.6%, while revenue guidance was nudged up 0.2%.
